blocks.text: New Delhi has denied any role in the plot to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Meanwhile, over 200 people have been hospitalized after consuming spurious liquor in Manipur state. DW has more.

items: Indian man is sentenced to 19 years in prison over plot to assassinate Sikh separatist leader
Over 200 people are hospitalized after consuming toxic liquor in Manipur state
India's men get a 118-run lead at stumps on day 3 of test against New Zealand

blocks.text: Here is a roundup of the main headlines from India on Saturday, November 21:
US judge jails Indian national in foiled plot to kill Sikh separatist, New Delhi denies involvement

blocks.caption: Gupta paid $15,000 to a person he thought was a hitman, but turned out to be an undercover US agentImage: Jane Rosenberg/REUTERS

blocks.text: A US federal judge sentenced an Indian national on Friday to 19 years and seven months in prison for plotting to hire a hitman to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.
Nikhil G.*, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
"I'm sorry to Mr. Pannun," he said in court. Judge Victor Marrero said he faces deportation to India after serving his sentence.
Prosecutors say an Indian government employee recruited the suspect in 2023. The government employee remains overseas and is not in US custody.
The defendant paid $15,000 (€13,670) to a person he believed was a hitman, who was actually an undercover US agent.
Prosecutors also said the defendant had told that agent the day after Hardeep Singh Nijjar's June 2023 killing in Canada that Nijjar "was also the target," the Associated Press reported.
His lawyer, Isabelle Kirshner, denied he had any role in the Nijjar killing.

"There is no question he was not the brains behind this operation," she said. Canada has separately alleged India arranged Nijjar's killing, and India dismissed that, with both countries expelling diplomats.
India-Canada row over Sikh killing has Punjab on edge
India denies any involvement in the Pannun plot. New Delhi has designated Pannun a terrorist.
Pannun, who leads the group Sikhs for Justice, called Gupta a foot soldier and said outside court: "I'm ready to face India's bullet if that is the price I have to pay."

blocks.caption: Sikhs for Justice (SFJ) wants an independent Khalistan state and has been banned by India Image: David R. Martin/AP Photo/picture alliance
